Short 08 · 2026-08-24 · Liquidity · Supply channel

Supply, habitat and the price of liquidity

Twenty-one years of Polish sovereign bond liquidity, treated for once as the thing to be explained rather than an input to something else. Supply prices in through the stock of a segment and its residual-maturity concentration, not through monthly issuance flow. The post-2020 foreign retreat is loud in price impact and silent in the capped quoted spread. And total debt loads on the term premium with a maturity gradient that has the textbook signature of preferred habitat, leaving a mark-to-market bill of about 2.5 percent of the sovereign market's present value from the 2019 to 2025 debt expansion.

Now accepted for publication
The paper behind this short, and behind the liquidity tab of this site, was accepted by Borsa Istanbul Review (Elsevier) on 24 August 2026 and is now in production. The published version will be open access.

A less-liquid sovereign market produces a daily fixing and a monthly turnover figure, not a tick tape. The paper builds the liquidity panel that this data reality allows: six low-frequency estimators plus the zero-trading-days share, computed bond by bond over 2005 to 2026, then asked what actually drives them. Three layers of evidence stack up: bond-month and segment-month panels with Driscoll-Kraay inference, event studies around MPC rate decisions and primary auctions, and a monthly regression of the aggregate spread and the ACM term premia on a supply-and-macro block.

Four findings carry the paper. First, issue size is the single most robust bond-level driver: bigger lines are cheaper to trade on every venue-uncapped measure. Second, the supply channel works through stocks, the size and residual-maturity concentration of what is outstanding, and not through the month-to-month pace of issuance. Third, the buy-side retreat after 2020, when the foreign share of PLN debt fell from about a third to under fifteen percent, is the strongest macro correlate of segment price impact, yet leaves the quoted spread untouched, because the regulated venue caps quotes by rule. Fourth, total State Treasury debt loads on the term premium with a gradient that rises from two to ten years, exactly where preferred-habitat theory puts it.

Figure · The preferred-habitat gradient: term-premium response to a 100 bn PLN rise in total debt

Response of the ACM term premium to a 100 bn PLN increase in total State Treasury debt, monthly regressions 2012:01 to 2025:12 with Newey-West inference, supply-and-macro controls included. The loading rises monotonically with maturity, the empirical signature of a preferred-habitat mechanism: supply pressure is priced where duration-constrained demand is least elastic. One and three asterisks mark significance at ten and one percent.

Counterfactual repricing of the sovereign universe (2026-04-21, face 952 bn PLN)PV (bn PLN)vs market
A · market curve (fitted NSS)949.8—
B · risk-neutral curve (no term premium)997.2+4.99%
C · market curve minus the estimated supply wedge972.7+2.41%

The table turns the gradient into money. Repricing every fixed-cash-flow Treasury bond on a curve stripped of the supply wedge accumulated over the 2019 to 2025 debt expansion lifts the market's present value by about 23 bn PLN, roughly two and a half percent. That is the standing mark-to-market bill of the expansion's term-premium component, distinct from the full term premium, which is worth about five percent. The auction event study adds the microstructure end of the same story: in the pre-2022 sample, secondary yields drift down one to three basis points in the two weeks after a primary auction, more at longer tenors, the classic dealer inventory-absorption pattern documented for US Treasuries.

The measurement lesson runs through everything. A venue that caps quoted spreads by rule makes the quoted spread a truncated statistic, so stress migrates to where it is not capped, into price impact per unit of volume. Any monitoring framework, and any cross-country comparison, that reads only quoted spreads will systematically flatter capped venues and miss episodes like the post-2020 foreign retreat entirely.

What this means for practitioners
For the issuer, consolidating borrowing into fewer and larger benchmark lines is the cheapest liquidity policy available, since stocks and concentration price in while monthly flow does not. For investors and risk managers, carry quote-based and volume-scaled liquidity measures in parallel, because under a spread cap the quoted number can sit still through a genuine liquidity deterioration. For the venue and its supervisor, mandatory market making narrows what is visible without removing what is priced.
Underlying paper · Dec, M. (2026). Supply, habitat and the price of liquidity in less-liquid sovereign bond markets. Evidence from Poland.
